commands: kubectl get pods -n test-social-network -o wide; kubectl get events -n test-social-network --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

kubectl describe pod user-service-5b549cc8dc-p2gkx -n test-social-network | tail -15; kubectl get deploy user-service -n test-social-network -o yaml | grep -n -A8 -i -E "nodeSelector|affinity|resources"

kubectl patch deploy user-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'; kubectl rollout status deploy/user-service -n test-social-network --timeout=90s
agent.summary:
**Problem:** The `user-service` pod was stuck in `Pending`. Its deployment had a `nodeSelector` of `kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node`, and the cluster has no node with that name. The only other node is the control plane, which has a taint. So the scheduler had nowhere to put the pod.

**Fix:** I removed the `nodeSelector` from the `user-service` deployment with a JSON patch. The rollout finished successfully. I didn't check the pod's status or test the service after the rollout.

The patch only touched the live deployment. The deployment is Helm-managed (release `social-network`), so a later `helm upgrade` could bring the bad `nodeSelector` back unless it is also fixed in the chart or values.
